data.turoyo: Bi dukṯayo di ṭayuṯo mǧadlone wayne, mḥarbone wayna ʕam u ʕamo nuxroyo, barbroyo lašan li ʕito səryayto, lašan u ʕamayḏan w i ǧamaʕayḏan das səroye, u ḥasyayḏa, aq qašayḏ́, aš šamošayḏa, ar rišonayḏa.
data.translation: In jenem Ort des Islams waren wir kämpferisch, wir waren kämpferisch gegen das fremde Volk der Barbarei für die syrische Kirche, für unser Volk und unsere Gemeinde, für die Aramäer: ihre Bischöfe, ihre Priester, ihre Meßdiener, seine Leiter.

rationale: New Part act. box: plural agentive mḥarbone with wayna, not finite Infectum mḥarbi.

summary: Reviewed all 52 occurrences. Existing (an)kämpfen covers military, individual and game combat; no new numbered sense or light-verb idiom is established.

Valency: ʕam/aʕm- normally gives opponent, including reciprocal ʕam ḥḏoḏe. 85/11 has mḥarbile with a suffixed opponent. Preterit l-marking can index full agent NPs, including coordinated l Nari w laš šawʕo aḥunone (96/264); 95/233 coordinates ele and l ʕAli Aġa. The cognate ḥarb at61/282 quantifies a fight rather than an opponent.

Aspect: bounded long fights use Preterit (95/110,248); narrative and iterative Infectum occur without -wa (69/553). Infectum-wa provides background duration (JTM3.2/38) and counterfactual gəmḥarabwa (60/190). Part act. mḥarbono/mḥarbone gives a fighter description.
Keep ḥrb II separate from related ḥwrb forms; the inherited etymology is preserved rather than replaced by readers' unproved Arabic-origin statements.

No example from Lahdo Traitor2/53 is added: Turoyo tre yarḥe says two months but the edition gives three, and mḥarabe may need morphological checking. Preserve the unfinished ʕam i... at32/9 without supplying an opponent.
Round 1 already filled Preterit and Infectum to five examples and Infectum-wa to four, and added Imperativ and Part act. No stale thin-cell proposal is repeated.
Counterfactual mḥarbinawo is coordinated with sayminawo and ṭəlbinawo under an unreal residence premise. Jan’s political comparison does not establish a separate activist sense.
The etymology and ḥrb II label remain inherited; the new forms do not support reassignment to ḥwrb.
Confirm -le opponent in85/11 beside ʕam; should government be made explicit in the gloss?
Confirm whether mḥarebu in91/25 is an Imperativ variant with m-, or a command using another form; no m- was silently removed.
Lahdo Traitor2/53 has tre yarḥe against the edition's three months. Correct the translation only after editorial source checking; also confirm mḥarabe form.
Who was intended after unfinished ʕam i... at32/9? The edition does not authorize filling it.
Existing ḥrb.II.t.infectum.3 and .infectum-wa.2 have citations embedded in translation rather than refs. Check parsing structure before altering source punctuation.
Should mqabəl d- be added explicitly to the government note for (an)kämpfen alongside ʕam and the opponent suffix? The one clear Jan attestation is retained.
Place-names stand for combatants, both subject (Bsorino) and opponent (walaye). A competitive game also uses the same ʕam-opponent construction; pest-control combat is already inherited at 1/30.
mqabəl d- encodes an opposing army alongside the earlier ʕam and suffix constructions; no new opposition sense.
A counterfactual collective rights struggle and historical military fighting share the existing combat meaning; duration and political purpose do not create new senses.
